claims.text: Existing hallucination detection techniques in language assistants rely on parameter-based or complex chain-of-thought methods that suffer from interpretability issues.
Post-generation hallucination identification methods cannot prevent hallucination occurrence.
Post-generation hallucination identification methods suffer from inconsistent performance due to instruction format and model style influences.
SELF-FAMILIARITY evaluates a model's familiarity with concepts present in the input instruction prior to response generation.
SELF-FAMILIARITY withholds response generation when unfamiliar concepts are detected in the input instruction.
SELF-FAMILIARITY demonstrates consistently superior performance compared to existing hallucination prevention techniques across four different large language models.

evidence.description: Validation of SELF-FAMILIARITY across four different large language models demonstrated consistently superior performance compared to existing techniques.

methodologies.name: SELF-FAMILIARITY
methodologies.description: A pre-detection self-evaluation technique that evaluates an LLM's familiarity with concepts in an input instruction and withholds response generation upon detecting unfamiliar concepts.
conditions: evaluated across four large language models

limitations.text: Existing techniques for hallucination detection rely on intricate fuzzy CoT or parameter-based methods that suffer from interpretability issues.
Methods that identify hallucinations post-generation cannot prevent their occurrence.
Post-generation methods suffer from inconsistent performance due to the influence of instruction format and model style.
